title: Saturation of a line in a free module over a DVR
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] with fraction field $K$, let $E$ be a finite free $R$-module of rank $r\ge1$, and let $0\ne s\in E\otimes_R K$. Inside $E\otimes_R K$ put $L:=E\cap Ks$. Then $L$ is finite free of rank one over $R$, the image of $L$ in $E\otimes_R K$ spans the line $Ks$, and $E/L$ is finite free of rank $r-1$ over $R$.

source.place: Tag 0CC4 (divisors-lemma-torsion-free-over-regular-dim-1), together with the elementary saturation calculation in the proof of the rank-induction paragraph of lem-sc-riemann-roch

proof.text: Choose an $R$-basis of $E$. Since $s\ne0$, some nonzero $a\in R$ clears the finitely many denominators of the coordinates of $s$ in $E\otimes_RK$, so $as\in E$; hence $L=E\cap Ks$ is nonzero. It is an $R$-submodule of $E$, and it is saturated: if $0\ne b\in R$ and $be\in L$ for $e\in E$, then $e=b^{-1}(be)\in Ks$, so $e\in L$.

source.place: Tag 0CC4, torsion-free intersection calculation in the proof of lemma-torsion-free-over-regular-dim-1

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-dvr-saturation-line-smith-normal-form] to the submodule $L\subseteq E$. It supplies bases in which the inclusion is diagonal, with $n\le r$ basis vectors for $L$. After tensoring with the fraction field $K$, the image of $L\otimes_RK$ is the $K$-span of the nonzero diagonal basis vectors. The clearing-denominator argument gives $Ks\subseteq L\otimes_RK$, while $L\subseteq Ks$ gives the reverse inclusion; therefore $L\otimes_RK=Ks$, which has $K$-dimension one. Thus exactly one diagonal factor occurs and $L$ has rank one; its image spans $Ks$.

source.place: Tag 0CC4, torsion-free-over-regular-dim-1 lemma, together with the rank-induction saturation paragraph of lem-sc-riemann-roch

proof.text: In the same diagonal bases, if a diagonal scalar were a nonunit, its class in $E/L$ would be nonzero and would be killed by that scalar. This cannot happen: if $0\ne b\in R$ and $be\in L$, saturation from step 1 gives $e\in L$. Hence every diagonal scalar is a unit. The quotient is therefore free on the remaining $r-1$ basis vectors, so $E/L$ is finite free of rank $r-1$.

lean.statement: theorem dvr_saturation_line {R K E : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsDiscreteValuationRing R] [Field K] [Algebra R K] [IsFractionRing R K] [AddCommGroup E] [Module R E] {r : ℕ} (b : Basis (Fin r) R E) (hr : 1 ≤ r) (s : E ⊗[R] K) (hs : s ≠ 0) : let V : Submodule K (K ⊗[R] E) := Submodule.span K {TensorProduct.comm R E K s} let i : E →ₗ[R] K ⊗[R] E := TensorProduct.mk R K E 1 let L : Submodule R E := (V.restrictScalars R).comap i Nonempty (Basis (Fin 1) R L) ∧ Submodule.span K (i '' (L : Set E)) = V ∧ Nonempty (Basis (Fin (r - 1)) R (E ⧸ L))
